It is cheap, but it cannot give any quality evidence. The gate's `GO_BOUNDED_ENCODER_DESIGN` label overstates what the gate showed. The first run that can say anything about quality is the separately frozen 100-update comparison, and prior art predicts it will come out negative.\n\n## Is the gate valid?\n\n1. **It could not have failed on the mechanism. It only failed on the prototype gain, which was already known.**\n   - wide256 and narrow128 are both frozen PCA of the pretrained cache, with no training. So +2.93pp only says that PCA dimensions 129\u2013256 carry fit-class information. The earlier 1024D panel already showed that at +3.32pp.\n   - The receipt shows the fold throws that information away. folded128 differs from narrow128 on only 2 of 512 queries, while wide256 gains 16 queries and loses 1. This follows from the method: the uncentered SVD of centred, normalized PCA256 outputs gives back the leading PCA128 subspace.\n   - So the folded floor (\u2265\u22121pp) was passed by construction. The whole route rests on an assumption the gate never tested: that training moves discriminative content into the **top-energy** 128 directions.\n   - ArcFace across about 2004 fit products tends to spread proxies evenly over the sphere. That flattens the output spectrum, and the folded 128 then drifts toward an arbitrary half of 256D.\n   - Matryoshka-style results (post-hoc SVD/PCA of wide embeddings loses to training natively at the low dimension) point the same way. That is the prior-art expectation, not a proposal to switch.\n2. **The 34.9% unused-gradient figure is close to tautological.**\n   - Wide head rows 129\u2013256 are orthogonal to the narrow rows by construction. Any nonzero ArcFace or bank gradient on those output coordinates therefore shows up outside the narrow span.\n   - It is measured against the frozen cached pooler output, not the encoder parameters.\n   - It points exactly at the directions the folded head will **not** read, unless the post-training SVD rotates onto them. It is evidence the extra coordinates are supervised, not that anything survives the fold.\n   - The two arms also start at different losses (5.80 vs 5.12 on batch 1), because 256D class-mean proxies separate more easily. The gradient regimes differ.\n   - The probe skips the rank term on batches containing singletons. The training script's inactive or valid-anchor handling differs from that, so the probe does not exactly replicate the training objective.\n3. **Relabel the receipt's meaning** as \"extra supervised coordinates exist and are finite,\" not \"capacity route viable.\"\n\n## Is the folding and export correct?\n\n- **The maths is correct.** `normalize(C\u00b7normalize(Wx+b)) = normalize(C(Wx+b))` holds because normalize is invariant to positive scaling. Folding the bias as `Cb` is right, and uncentered is the right choice because centring would not commute. The float64 fixture and the float32 error of 1.4e-6 cover this.\n- **Keep three things separate:**\n  - (a) the mathematical identity, which is proven;\n  - (b) float association, i.e. two matmuls vs one folded matmul, which differs by about 1e-6 and should never be promised bit-exact;\n  - (c) packed exactness: int8 rounding flips near the .5 boundary are expected, so measure a flip rate and don't assert zero. fp16_native serving adds a separate error, and the reference for it is the existing serving parity receipts.\n- **New packing risk.** The leading uncentered singular vector picks up any mean offset once the trained bias drifts. With `fixed_int8_unit_codes` using a fixed scale, one dominant coordinate reduces resolution for all the others. Record the per-coordinate |max| distribution, the clamp count, and packed-vs-float top-1 agreement for folded128 against native128.\n- **Serving fails closed, which is good.** `siglip2_compact_serving.py:227` loads `nn.Linear(1024,128)` strictly, so a raw 256 checkpoint cannot be served by accident.\n\n## Must fix before the smoke\n\n1. **Dimension authority.**\n   - `compact_head_features` rejects `output_dim` 256 (`src/sfora/sop_compact_training.py:39`). Widen that allowlist to exactly {128, 256}; don't bypass it.\n   - `masks = torch.arange(128)` (`train_inshop_siglip2_unseen_gallery.py:600`) must become `arange(head.out_features)`.\n   - The bank width must follow the head.\n   - Build the wide head by reusing the probe's construction, with the assertion `pca.components[:128] == narrow.weight`. Don't change `OUTPUT_WIDTH`.\n   - Add a single `--head-width {128,256}`, allowed only for `freeze_emb`, seed 179024, updates \u2208 {17, 100}. Record `head_width` in the checkpoint and receipt.\n2. **Pixel identity.**\n   - `first_input_batch_sha256` is only recorded for `step <= 10` (line 614). Record it for all 17 steps and require the two arms to match exactly.\n   - Constructing `nn.Linear(1024,256)` consumes global torch RNG. Fork the RNG or construct the layer before seeding, and prove that loader and augmentation streams are identical.\n3. **Native control reproduction.** Re-run native128 fresh through the new code path, since `source_manifest` hashes change. It must match the existing freeze_emb/179024/17-update loss trajectory. Never reuse the old receipt as the control.\n4. **Clipping confound.** Global `clip_grad_norm_(\u2026, 1.0)` (line 728) includes head and classifier gradients, and those grow with width. That changes the encoder's effective step size. Log pre-clip norms per group (vision, head, classifier) and the clip factor for every step.\n5. **Other width confounds to log, not fix:**\n   - ArcFace at s=64 over a 256D cosine distribution;\n   - the smooth-AP bank sigmoid temperature was tuned for 128D, where random-pair cosine spread is about 1/\u221ad;\n   - AdamW weight decay applies to twice as many head and classifier parameters;\n   - the proxy initial scale and separability differ.\n6. **Fit-only compactor semantics.** Define these in the frozen document before running:\n   - trained encoder in eval mode, with the serving preprocess path (`_direct_preprocess` as in the parity receipts);\n   - fp32 with TF32 off, fit rows only, and no augmentation;\n   - a deterministic float64 SVD with the sign rule, and a rank check \u03c3\u2081\u2082\u2088 > 1e-10;\n   - the compactor SHA and the full singular spectrum recorded, including retained energy \u03a3\u03c3\u00b2\u2081..\u2081\u2082\u2088/\u03a3\u03c3\u00b2 as the isotropy diagnostic;\n   - compactor frozen before any held read.\n\n## Smoke pass criteria (mechanics only, \u2264120 s per arm, no held read)\n\n- All 17 steps finite, no scaler-skipped steps, and all parameters finite at the end.\n- Wide/native median ratios logged for per-group pre-clip norm and clip factor. Kill if the encoder-group share moves by more than 2\u00d7.\n- Cost: median wide step time \u2264 1.05\u00d7 native, and peak CUDA memory \u2264 native + 1 GiB.\n- **Folded reload:**\n  - Fit the compactor on a preregistered fixed fit subset (for example the first 2048 fit-order rows; rank must be \u2265128).\n  - Save `{vision, head: 1024\u2192128}` in the standard schema and load it through `Siglip2CompactEncoder.from_checkpoint` in fp32_autocast.\n  - On 64 fixed fit images:\n    - reloaded vs in-process folded floats: max error \u2264 1e-5, and packed bytes identical;\n    - two-stage-then-pack vs folded-then-pack: int8 flip rate reported, with every flip \u2264 1 LSB.\n  - The raw 256 checkpoint must be rejected by the serving loader.\n- Report the uncentered retained energy, the top-coordinate magnitude and the int8 clamp count.\n\n## The 100-update gate a positive smoke would authorize (freeze it separately)\n\n- Compare native128 against folded128, both TRAIN-held and packed. Fit the compactor on all fit rows after training. Report mAP@R and R1 with paired product-bootstrap 95% intervals. wide256 is never scored on held.\n- **Continue** only if folded \u2212 native mAP@R \u2265 +0.5pp with a lower bound > 0, and the R1 point estimate \u2265 0.\n- **Kill** if the mAP point estimate is < 0.
